title: 4 Keys Keyboard
statement:
A keyboard has only four keys:

- `A` adds one letter A to the end of the screen.
- `Ctrl-A` selects all text on the screen.
- `Ctrl-C` copies the selected text into the clipboard, replacing what the clipboard held.
- `Ctrl-V` adds the clipboard's contents to the end of the screen.

The screen and the clipboard start empty, and adding text never replaces a selection. Given `n`, return the largest number of A's the screen can show after at most `n` key presses.
notes:
## Intuition

A brute-force search over every key sequence works for small `n` but grows exponentially. Look at how an optimal sequence ends instead. Either the last press is `A`, or the sequence finishes with a block "`Ctrl-A`, `Ctrl-C`, then some `Ctrl-V`s". In the second case, if the first `j` presses leave the most A's possible, `dp[j]`, and the remaining `i - j` presses are `Ctrl-A`, `Ctrl-C` and `i - j - 2` pastes, the screen ends with `dp[j] * (i - j - 1)` letters: the original text plus one copy per paste. The best answer for `i` presses is the largest of these choices, built from smaller answers.

## Approach

1. `dp[i]` is the most A's after at most `i` presses; `dp[0] = 0`.
2. For each `i` from 1 to `n`, start with `dp[i] = dp[i - 1] + 1` (the last press types an `A`).
3. For each split `j` from 1 to `i - 3`, try ending with `Ctrl-A`, `Ctrl-C` and `i - j - 2` pastes: `dp[j] * (i - j - 1)`.
4. Keep the maximum and return `dp[n]`.

## Example 1, step by step

`n = 3`. `dp[1] = 1`, `dp[2] = 2` and `dp[3] = 3`: for these `i` the inner loop does not run (`i - 3 < 1`), because selecting and copying already uses two presses and a paste needs a third, after at least one typed letter. The answer is `3`. For comparison, at `i = 7` the split `j = 3` gives `3 * (7 - 3 - 1) = 9`, beating the 7 from typing.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n²): each `i` tries up to `i - 3` splits.
- Space: O(n) for `dp`.

## Pitfalls

- `Ctrl-A` and `Ctrl-C` cost two presses, so `k` pastes multiply by `k + 1`, giving the factor `i - j - 1`, not `i - j`.
- Until `n = 6` plain typing is best, so `dp[i - 1] + 1` must remain a candidate.
- Several rounds of copy and paste can be chained; the `dp[j]` factor already includes the best earlier rounds.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `dp[i]` | most A's possible with at most `i` presses |
| `i` | number of presses being solved |
| `j` | presses used before the final `Ctrl-A`, `Ctrl-C`, pastes block |

narration.2: dp[i] will hold the most A's reachable with i presses; dp[0] is 0.
narration.3: Solve every press count from 1 up to n, smallest first.
narration.4: One option: the last press types a single A.
narration.5: Other option: after j presses, spend the rest on Ctrl-A, Ctrl-C and at least one paste.
narration.6: The i - j - 2 pastes add that many copies of dp[j], for dp[j] * (i - j - 1) in total.
narration.9: dp[n] is the best result with n presses.
